cta.label: Request an Appointment
cta.text: Please feel welcome to contact our friendly reception staff with any general or medical enquiry. Our doctors will receive or return any urgent calls.

hero.title: A dentist can make your smile great.
hero.lead: Quality care in a state of the art facility. To see for yourself, visit us and get a consultation from one of our highly trained and experienced dentists.
points: A doctor on call for emergencies

overview.title: Complete dental services for the highest patient demands, tailored for each case.
overview.text: General dentistry covers a wide range of procedures. The goal of general dentistry is to remove all disease from your mouth.

services.title: Emergency Dentistry
services.summary: Same-day care for urgent dental pain.
services.text: Same-day appointments for severe toothache, cracked or knocked-out teeth, swelling, abscesses and lost fillings or crowns.
services.lead: When sudden tooth pain or a dental injury occurs, you need quick, reliable care. We provide same-day dental appointments in Pasadena to restore your comfort and peace of mind, for both adults and children.

covers.title: What we treat the same day
covers.text: Severe or persistent toothaches, cracked, broken or chipped teeth, knocked-out or loose teeth from trauma, swollen gums and dental abscesses, lost fillings, crowns or veneers, and gum infections and bleeding.

covers.title: Before you reach the clinic
covers.text: For tooth pain, rinse with warm water and apply a cold compress. For a knocked-out tooth, keep it moist in milk or saliva and bring it with you. For swelling or infection, avoid heat and call the office right away. For broken restorations, save any pieces.

covers.title: Flexible scheduling
covers.text: We know emergencies do not wait for business hours, so we keep room in the schedule for urgent cases, whether it is early morning or late in the day.

covers.title: Cost and coverage
covers.text: We accept most insurance plans and provide flexible payment options for emergency treatment.

questions.q: What is considered a dental emergency?
questions.a: A dental emergency includes severe pain, swelling, broken teeth, abscesses, or bleeding that won't stop.

questions.q: Can I get a same-day dental appointment in Pasadena?
questions.a: Yes. We offer same-day appointments for urgent cases like tooth pain, broken fillings, or dental trauma.

questions.q: What should I do if I have a knocked-out tooth?
questions.a: Keep the tooth moist in milk or saline solution and contact our office immediately. Quick action increases the chance of saving your tooth.

questions.q: Do you offer after-hours emergency dentistry?
questions.a: If you have an urgent issue after hours, call our office and we will arrange the earliest possible appointment to address your emergency.

services.title: Dental Exams
services.summary: Check-ups, cleanings and oral cancer screening.
services.text: A full examination of teeth, gums, bite and jaw joint, with professional cleaning, X-rays where needed and an oral cancer screening.
services.lead: Maintaining excellent oral health starts with regular dental exams. Each exam is personalised to your own needs, taking account of your medical history, oral hygiene practices and specific concerns.

covers.title: Review of your history
covers.text: We begin by reviewing your dental and medical history to understand your overall health and identify anything that may affect your care.

covers.title: Visual examination and X-rays
covers.text: We examine your teeth, gums, tongue and oral tissues for decay, gum disease and signs of teeth grinding or jaw joint problems, and take X-rays where areas are not visible.

covers.title: Gum evaluation
covers.text: We measure the depth of the gum pockets around your teeth, which helps in diagnosing and monitoring gum disease.

covers.title: Professional cleaning
covers.text: An exam typically includes a professional cleaning to remove plaque and tartar buildup, which helps prevent tooth decay and gum disease.

covers.title: Oral cancer screening
covers.text: Every regular exam includes a thorough oral cancer screening, because early detection significantly increases the chances of successful treatment.

covers.title: Exams for children
covers.text: We also offer dental exams for children, emphasising early dental care and education to establish good oral hygiene habits from a young age.

services.title: Cavity Filling
services.text: Decay removed and the tooth filled with composite resin, amalgam or porcelain, then shaped and polished to blend with the teeth beside it.
services.lead: A cavity, also known as dental caries or tooth decay, occurs when harmful bacteria in the mouth produce acids that attack the tooth's enamel. Left untreated, cavities can progress deeper into the tooth, leading to pain, infection and even tooth loss.

covers.title: Comprehensive examination
covers.text: We examine your teeth, gums and overall oral health, and may take X-rays to determine the extent of the cavity and assess any damage.

covers.title: Treatment plan
covers.text: We discuss the available options and recommend the filling material best suited to your cavity.

covers.title: Anesthesia and sedation
covers.text: Several anesthesia and sedation options are offered so you stay comfortable throughout the procedure.

covers.title: Filling and finishing
covers.text: The decayed portion is removed, the area cleaned, and the cavity filled with composite resin, amalgam or porcelain, then shaped and polished for a natural blend.

covers.title: Post-treatment care
covers.text: You get detailed instructions on oral hygiene and diet, and regular check-ups and cleanings keep the filling sound.

services.title: Root Canals
services.summary: Saving an infected tooth rather than pulling it.
services.text: Endodontic treatment that clears bacteria from an infected root canal, prevents reinfection and saves the natural tooth.
services.lead: Root canal treatment removes the inflamed or infected pulp, then the inside of the tooth is carefully cleaned, disinfected, filled and sealed. It eliminates bacteria from the infected root canal, prevents reinfection and saves the natural tooth.

covers.title: When a root canal is needed
covers.text: A cracked tooth from injury or genetics, a deep cavity, or problems from a previous filling. Signs include severe pain when chewing or biting, lingering sensitivity to hot or cold, swollen or tender gums, pimples on the gums, tooth discolouration and a loose tooth.

covers.title: How to prepare
covers.text: Take any antibiotics or anti-inflammatory medication as prescribed, avoid tobacco in the days beforehand, and eat a meal before the appointment, since the local anesthesia will numb your mouth for a few hours.

covers.title: The procedure
covers.text: Local anesthesia, a dental dam to isolate and dry the tooth, an access hole, removal of the pulp, cleaning and shaping of the canals, filling with gutta-percha and a temporary seal.

covers.title: The final restoration
covers.text: In most cases a crown protects the treated tooth and restores your bite. Crowns are made to measure and usually take two to three weeks, after which the temporary filling is replaced.

covers.title: Why it is worth doing
covers.text: It prevents the infection spreading to other teeth, relieves the symptoms of an infected tooth, reduces the risk of jawbone damage and avoids an extraction.

questions.q: How long does root canal treatment take?
questions.a: Depending on the amount of infection, treatment may need one or two appointments. On average a root canal takes about 30 to 60 minutes; a larger tooth with more than one root may take up to an hour and a half.

questions.q: What is the alternative to a root canal?
questions.a: The only alternative is extraction. If you are not a good candidate for root canal treatment, the tooth may be extracted and replaced with a dental implant, a bridge or a partial.

questions.q: How long do the results last?
questions.a: As with all dental procedures, results are not guaranteed. When root canal therapy is performed correctly, results can last a long time, even the rest of your life.

services.title: Implant Dentistry
services.summary: Titanium implants that replace missing teeth.
services.text: Implants placed in the jawbone to act as the roots of missing teeth, supporting a single crown, a bridge or a full denture.
services.lead: Implants are surgically placed in your jawbone, where they serve as the roots of missing teeth. Because the titanium fuses with the bone, they will not slip, make noise or cause the bone damage that fixed bridgework or dentures might, and the materials cannot decay.

covers.title: Types we place
covers.text: A single tooth dental implant, an implant-supported bridge and an implant-supported denture, including the all-on-four approach for a complete set.

covers.title: Who implants suit
covers.text: People with one or more missing teeth, a fully developed jaw, enough bone to hold the implant, healthy oral tissues and no condition that would interfere with bone healing, who are willing to commit several months to the process.

covers.title: Planning the treatment
covers.text: A complete dental examination with X-rays and 3D images, models of your teeth and jaw, a review of your medical history and medication, and a plan built around how many teeth are being replaced.

covers.title: What to expect
covers.text: Implant surgery is usually outpatient and done in stages, with healing time between them: removal of a damaged tooth, bone grafting where needed, implant placement, then abutments and the final crown, bridge or denture.

covers.title: Afterwards
covers.text: Swelling of the gums and face, some pain at the implant site and slight bleeding are normal, and pain medication or antibiotics may be needed. A soft diet helps while the site heals.

questions.q: How long does the implant fuse to the bone?
questions.a: A dental implant is placed in the jaw and comes into contact with the bone within three to six months.

questions.q: Do implants affect the teeth next to them?
questions.a: No. Unlike a dental bridge, implants do not require the alteration of adjacent teeth, which helps preserve your natural teeth and prevents bone loss in the jaw.

services.title: Laser Gum Therapy
services.text: Laser-Assisted New Attachment Procedure, which removes diseased gum tissue without sutures or scalpels and encourages lost tissue to regrow.
services.lead: Most adults have some form of gum disease, and the risk increases with age. Without proper care, periodontal disease can weaken and destroy the bone that supports your teeth. Laser surgery removes diseased or damaged tissue from around the gums without the use of sutures or scalpels.

covers.title: Why a laser
covers.text: As a less invasive option to traditional oral surgery, laser surgery leads to faster healing, reduces the risk of bleeding, has negligible post-operative discomfort and requires no downtime.

covers.title: Who it suits
covers.text: People with periodontitis are the best candidates. Patients with mouth sores from chemotherapy can also find relief with LANAP.

covers.title: The LANAP steps
covers.text: Assessment by probing the gums, laser sanitising to eliminate infection-causing bacteria, ultrasonic scaling to remove plaque and tartar, laser reconnection of gum tissue to the root, and grinding of certain sections of the tooth to prevent new tartar forming.

covers.title: How long it takes
covers.text: A single quadrant can be finished in one to two hours. A whole mouth may need two visits of one to two hours each.

covers.title: Side effects and recovery
covers.text: Light bleeding, slight swelling and partial gum discolouration are the usual effects, and they should disappear within 24 hours. Gum tissue itself takes a couple of weeks to grow back.

covers.title: After the therapy
covers.text: Eat soft but nutritious food while recovering and stay away from very hot or spicy meals, gum, hard candy, cookies and chips. Brushing twice a day, cleaning between the gums daily and rinsing with an antimicrobial mouth rinse keep the infection from returning.

services.title: Dental Brackets
services.text: Metal or ceramic brackets bonded to the teeth and worked with archwires and elastics to move teeth into position, for teens and adults.
services.lead: Dental brackets, also known as braces, are orthodontic devices used to correct dental alignment issues. Small metal or ceramic brackets are bonded to the front surface of the teeth and work with archwires, elastics and other components to apply gentle pressure.

covers.title: Initial consultation
covers.text: A visual examination, X-rays and impressions to assess the position of your teeth and jaw, and a conversation about your treatment goals.

covers.title: Treatment plan
covers.text: A plan tailored to your case, including which type of dental bracket suits it best.

covers.title: Placement and adjustment
covers.text: The brackets are bonded with a dental adhesive and connected by an archwire. Periodic appointments adjust and tighten the wire to keep progress steady.

covers.title: Maintenance and hygiene
covers.text: Detailed instructions on brushing technique, flossing method and diet while the brackets are on, with regular check-ups to monitor progress.

covers.title: Completion and retention
covers.text: Once the teeth have reached the desired alignment the brackets come off and a retainer, removable or fixed, holds the result.

covers.title: Other orthodontic options
covers.text: Alongside brackets we offer Invisalign clear aligners, retainers and other advanced treatment options.

services.title: Tooth Whitening
services.text: Professional whitening that lightens the colour of the teeth, with the before and after shade measured against a standard shade guide.
services.lead: Tooth whitening is any process that lightens the colour of a tooth, by removing the stain or by a chemical reaction. The active ingredient in most whitening products is hydrogen peroxide, delivered as hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide. We offer both in-office treatment and home-based options.

covers.title: In-office whitening
covers.text: A significant colour change in a short period. High-quality peroxide gel is applied by the dentist after the gums are protected with a paint-on rubber dam, and stays on the teeth for several 15 to 20 minute intervals adding up to about an hour.

covers.title: Take-home trays
covers.text: A fitted tray holding carbamide peroxide gel, worn for two to four hours a day or overnight. Whitening is usually noticeable within a few days, lightening teeth by one or two shades.

covers.title: What causes discolouration
covers.text: Red wine, coffee, tea, cola and other deep-coloured food and drink, acidic food that erodes enamel, smoking and chewing tobacco, teeth grinding, a high intake of fluoride in childhood, trauma to developing teeth, aging and certain medical treatments.

covers.title: How much lighter
covers.text: Before and after colour is assessed with a shade guide. Treatment can occasionally lighten teeth by nine or more shades, but most people who have their teeth bleached see a change of two to seven shades.

covers.title: The risks
covers.text: Increased tooth sensitivity and mild gum irritation are the commonly reported effects, and both are related to the concentration of the peroxide and the length of treatment. Sensitivity usually occurs during treatment and can last several days.

covers.title: Keeping the result
covers.text: At-home maintenance whitening, avoiding dark-coloured food and drink for at least a week afterwards, sipping dark drinks through a straw, and brushing and flossing after meals and at bedtime.

services.title: Under Sedation
services.summary: Nitrous oxide, oral and IV sedation.
services.text: Sedation dentistry for patients with dental anxiety, a low pain threshold or extensive treatment ahead of them.
services.lead: Dental anxiety or fear can be a significant barrier to receiving necessary dental treatment. Our team is trained in administering sedation techniques, so you can have the care you need in a relaxed state.

covers.title: Nitrous oxide
covers.text: Laughing gas, a mild sedative given through a small mask over your nose. It relaxes you while you stay conscious and responsive, and wears off quickly once the mask is removed.

covers.title: Oral conscious sedation
covers.text: Prescribed medication taken before the appointment for a deeper state of relaxation while you can still talk to the dental team. Bring a companion, as the effects may last a few hours.

covers.title: IV sedation
covers.text: Given directly into the bloodstream for precise control over the level of sedation. It induces a deep state of relaxation, and your vital signs are monitored closely throughout.

covers.title: Who it helps
covers.text: Patients who experience dental anxiety, who have a low pain threshold or heightened sensitivity, or who need complex or lengthy treatment that sedation lets us complete in a single appointment.

services.title: Radiology Service
services.summary: Digital X-rays, panoramic imaging and CBCT.
services.text: Dental imaging that finds cavities, bone loss, impacted teeth and other problems a routine examination cannot see.
services.lead: Dental radiography uses X-rays to create images of the teeth, bones and the soft tissue around them. These images let us detect cavities, tooth decay, bone loss, impacted teeth and other abnormalities at an early stage.

covers.title: Bitewing X-rays
covers.text: Used to detect decay between the teeth and changes in bone density caused by gum disease.

covers.title: Periapical X-rays
covers.text: A complete view of a single tooth from crown to root, which helps diagnose problems with the root and the bone around it.

covers.title: Occlusal X-rays
covers.text: Taken to capture the placement and development of an entire arch of teeth in the upper or lower jaw.

covers.title: Panoramic X-rays
covers.text: A broad view of the whole mouth, including teeth, jaws and surrounding structures, useful for impacted teeth, tumours, cysts and jaw disorders.

covers.title: Cephalometric X-rays
covers.text: A side view of the head used mainly in orthodontics, showing the relationship between teeth, jaw and facial profile.

covers.title: Cone beam CT
covers.text: Three-dimensional images of the dental structures, soft tissue, nerve paths and bone, particularly useful for implant planning and assessing bone structure and density.

questions.q: How much radiation does a dental X-ray involve?
questions.a: Our radiology equipment follows strict safety standards to minimise exposure, and digital X-rays in particular emit significantly lower radiation than traditional film X-rays.

services.title: Kids Dentistry
services.summary: Check-ups, sealants and care for children.
services.text: Preventive and restorative care for children in a welcoming, stress-free environment, with staff trained to work with young patients.
services.lead: A child's first dental experiences can shape their attitude towards oral health for a lifetime. Our pediatric-focused dental team provides a welcoming, stress-free environment where children can feel comfortable and confident during every visit.

covers.title: Preventive care
covers.text: Thorough cleanings, fluoride treatments and dental sealants to protect the teeth from decay. Sealants have been shown to significantly reduce the risk of cavities in children's permanent molars.

covers.title: Restorative treatment
covers.text: Cavity prevention, tooth-coloured fillings and emergency dental care for children.

covers.title: Education for children and parents
covers.text: Personalised oral hygiene education for both children and parents, so good habits start at home.

covers.title: A calm first visit
covers.text: Children are greeted with friendly faces and engaging activities that help ease their anxiety, and our staff is specially trained to work with them.

covers.title: Working with orthodontists
covers.text: Our team works closely with orthodontic specialists so a child's care is joined up when alignment needs attention.

about.title: A family dental practice on Shaver Street in Pasadena.
text: If you are looking for a dentist in Pasadena, Texas, Lone Star Family Dental is the place to go. A favourable location close to your home or work matters, because dental treatment involves more than a few appointments, and being an affordable dental office matters too.

Our experienced dentists and staff offer comprehensive dental exams and a wide array of general, preventative, cosmetic and other dental services, using state-of-the-art equipment. We provide adequate oral care to you and your loved ones in a warm and cosy atmosphere.

Our doctors have a wealth of knowledge about teeth and oral hygiene. They seek to educate their patients about proper dental care as well as the treatments suggested, and encourage them to develop good preventative care habits. Patients have access to their records and all the options for treatment are explained, because a patient needs to feel in control of their own care.

Our dentists pursue continuing education opportunities to keep abreast of new research and changing technology. Our experts have served this community, and they look forward to seeing you through many years down the line.

values.title: Never rushed
values.text: An office with a welcoming atmosphere, where patients never feel rushed or uncomfortable and the whole staff is friendly and helpful.

values.title: You decide
values.text: We involve patients in the decisions about their treatment, give them access to their records and explain every option before anything starts.

values.title: Modern equipment
values.text: Whatever your plan is, our state of the art equipment makes it simple for our team to make it a reality, just as you desire.

values.title: Emergency ready
values.text: A dental emergency can be a very traumatising experience, which is why we always have a doctor on call, ready to address it.

steps.title: Tell us what you need
steps.text: Call the office or send the appointment form with your name, phone, email and the date you would like.

steps.title: An examination first
steps.text: We review your dental and medical history, examine the teeth, gums and bite, and take X-rays where something is not visible.

steps.title: The plan, explained
steps.text: We talk through what we found and recommend the treatment, answering your questions before anything is agreed.

steps.title: Treatment and aftercare
steps.text: Treatment goes ahead with the sedation option you chose, and you leave with instructions for looking after it.

faqs.q: How do I book an appointment?
faqs.a: Call the office or send the appointment form with your name, email, phone, the date you would like and a note for the doctor. Our doctors will receive or return any urgent calls.
We accept most insurance plans, and you can ask the office about your benefits when you book.

faqs.q: What if I do not have dental insurance?
faqs.a: Having no dental insurance does not mean you should postpone care. Ask us about self-pay pricing, payment arrangements, treatment alternatives where they are clinically appropriate, and whether treatment can be staged.

faqs.q: Will I know what treatment costs before it starts?
faqs.a: We discuss financial responsibility before treatment. A pretreatment estimate helps you understand potential costs, though an estimate is not always a guarantee of payment.
Yes. We offer dental exams for children and a full range of pediatric services, from preventive care to restorative treatment.

faqs.q: What can I do about dental anxiety?
faqs.a: We offer nitrous oxide, oral conscious sedation and IV sedation, and we will go through which suits you based on your medical history, dental needs and anxiety level.

facts.heading: Emergencies
facts.text: We always have a doctor on call, ready to address emergencies, and we keep room for same-day appointments. If you have an urgent issue after hours, call the office and we will arrange the earliest possible appointment.
